items.title: Sample card — GitHub result
items.summary: Real harvests put the repository name here, with its description, star count and primary language underneath.
items.angle: Claude writes this line: one concrete tool you could build off the back of the finding.

items.title: Sample card — blog post surfaced via Hacker News
items.angle: Blog and long-form finds come through the Hacker News search index, which is free and needs no key.

items.title: Sample card — Reddit thread
items.summary: Threads are filtered to the past year and to posts with a few upvotes, so the board isn't flooded with noise.
items.angle: Practitioner complaints are the richest seam here — they name the tool that doesn't exist yet.

items.title: Sample card — preprint
items.summary: arXiv is queried by recency rather than relevance, so papers arrive before the methods reach commercial software.
items.angle: A method published without an implementation is the clearest possible brief for a small tool.

items.title: Sample card — save this one to test
items.summary: Hit Save, then reload the page. It should still be saved. Export writes the saved set to a JSON file you can keep or move to another device.

items.title: Sample card — these all disappear on the first real run
items.summary: The harvester strips any card marked as a sample before writing new results, so you don't have to clean up.
